title: PrivFusion: Privacy-Preserving Model Fusion via Decentralized Federated Graph Matching
authors: ["Qian Chen", "Yiqiang Chen", "Xinlong Jiang", "Teng Zhang", "Weiwei Dai", "Wuliang Huang", "Bingjie Yan", "Zhen Yan", "Wang Lu", "Bo Ye"]
venue_full_name: IEEE Transactions on Knowledge and Data Engineering
research_problem: Fuse independently trained models while limiting disclosure of model activations and weights to other model owners.
key_idea: PrivFusion combines locally perturbed graph representations, decentralized neuron matching, and a perturbation-filter adapter. Mechanistic reading is from the differently titled 2023 author preprint, not the 2024 version of record.
technical_mechanism: Author preprint arXiv:2311.03396v1, Sections III–IV: represent neurons/channels as nodes and weights as edges; perturb activation features with Laplace noise and bounded weight features with a multi-bit mechanism; combine activation/weight affinities for graph matching; align neurons, apply Gaussian perturbation and smoothing, and average aligned weights.
assumptions: Author preprint: honest-but-curious model owners; agreed tasks and compatible public architectures; aligned input/output neurons; a few inference examples to obtain activation features; bounded weight features and calibrated sensitivities/privacy budgets. The fusion stage avoids retraining but is not strictly data-free.
main_contribution: A decentralized privacy-aware graph-matching fusion procedure, with author-stated local-DP mechanisms and privacy–utility experiments on image tasks and a two-party healthcare construction.
limitations: Content reviewed in arXiv:2311.03396v1 only; the final TKDE text was not accessed. Small-network evaluations and graph-matching memory cost limit scalability evidence. The healthcare data originate from 17 hospitals but the reported experiment groups 15 regions into two parties; this is not evidence of a live 17-hospital federation. Strong regional heterogeneity can degrade fusion substantially (preprint Table IV). Privacy unit, sensitivity calibration, approximate-DP delta, and composition across releases require explicit accounting before asserting end-to-end patient-level privacy.

title: DIMAT: Decentralized Iterative Merging-And-Training for Deep Learning Models
authors: ["Nastaran Saadati", "Minh Pham", "Nasla Saleem", "Joshua R. Waite", "Aditya Balu", "Zhanong Jiang", "Chinmay Hegde", "Soumik Sarkar"]
venue_full_name: IEEE/CVF Conference on Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition
research_problem: Decentralized parameter averaging can combine misaligned neurons and converge slowly under heterogeneous data.
key_idea: Alternate local optimization with activation-based neuron matching and merging among neighboring models.
technical_mechanism: Activation matching produces layerwise permutation matrices by a linear assignment problem; neighbors are aligned before weighted combination, and the procedure interleaves these merge steps with local SGD or adaptive optimization.
assumptions: Compatible model layers, data for activation matching and local optimization, and a connected communication graph; convergence analysis assumes smoothness, bounded stochastic/heterogeneity terms and a spectral condition on the combined mixing/permutation operator.

title: Breaking the Aggregation Bottleneck in Federated Recommendation: A Personalized Model Merging Approach

technical_mechanism: A local MLP generates item-specific mixing weights from local embeddings and global/local differences. title: FedAWA: Adaptive Optimization of Aggregation Weights in Federated Learning Using Client Vectors
authors: ["Changlong Shi", "He Zhao", "Bingjie Zhang", "Mingyuan Zhou", "Dandan Guo", "Yi Chang"]
venue_full_name: IEEE/CVF Conference on Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition
research_problem: Fixed client aggregation weights can neglect client-update directions under heterogeneous data.
key_idea: Optimize aggregation coefficients from the geometric alignment of client vectors.
technical_mechanism: FedAWA subtracts the incoming global model from each locally trained model, optimizes normalized client coefficients to align the merged update with client vectors, and adds alignment to the current global model; a layer-wise variant chooses coefficients separately by layer.
assumptions: Common compatible model coordinates, iterative client training and a server able to inspect client updates; runtime weighting does not require a separate validation/proxy dataset.
main_contribution: Uses update geometry to adapt server aggregation weights without extra runtime proxy examples.
limitations: The method still requires local training and repeated communication. Directional alignment is a proxy for generalization; raw update access is not automatically compatible with secure aggregation, and no formal privacy or demographic-fairness guarantee follows from it.

title: Many-Task Federated Fine-Tuning via Unified Task Vectors
authors: ["Vasileios Tsouvalas", "Tanir Ozcelebi", "Nirvana Meratnia"]
venue_full_name: Workshop on Federated Learning in the Age of Generative AI (FedGenAI), co-located with IJCAI 2025
research_problem: Clients with multiple distinct tasks can make per-task or per-client model storage and communication expensive.
key_idea: Compress each client’s task updates into one unified vector and reconstruct task behavior with lightweight modulators.
technical_mechanism: MaTU unifies task-vector signs and magnitudes, sends the resulting vector plus binary masks and rescalers, and aggregates same-task and selected cross-task information according to known client/task assignments and sign compatibility.
assumptions: Shared pretrained backbone and compatible task vectors, local per-task fine-tuning, known task assignments at the server, and communicated masks/rescalers.
main_contribution: Offers a compact representation for iterative many-task federated adaptation without retaining a separate server model for every client.
limitations: Task labels, masks and updates may disclose information; local data retention is not a formal privacy guarantee. Experiments on 30 benchmark datasets do not establish live cross-institution federation. This is a companion-workshop paper and does not inherit IJCAI A.

title: DENSE: Data-Free One-Shot Federated Learning
authors: ["Jie Zhang", "Chen Chen", "Bo Li", "Lingjuan Lyu", "Shuang Wu", "Shouhong Ding", "Chunhua Shen", "Chao Wu"]
venue_full_name: Conference on Neural Information Processing Systems
research_problem: One-shot federation needs to combine heterogeneous client models without a shared auxiliary dataset or repeated client communication.
key_idea: Generate synthetic inputs from uploaded models, then distill their averaged logits into a server student.
technical_mechanism: Train a server generator using ensemble classification, batch-normalization statistics and a teacher-student boundary-disagreement objective; alternate generation and KL-based ensemble-to-student distillation after the client models are uploaded once.
assumptions: Server access to client models and their BN statistics for the stated generation loss, compatible input/output-label semantics and server-side generation/distillation compute; raw auxiliary examples are not required at the server.
main_contribution: Supplies a one-shot behavioral-fusion route across differing architectures and a contrast to coordinate averaging or curvature-weighted fusion.
limitations: Data-free refers to the absence of raw auxiliary training data at the server, not absence of local training data, BN statistics or server optimization. Visual dissimilarity of generated images does not establish privacy: the paper leaves additional privacy mechanisms and attack analysis for future work. Model access and synthesis quality remain substantive assumptions.
